CBSA.CICSBSA.ABNDFILE.recovery_why: etc/install/base/installjcl/BANK.csd: DEFINE FILE(ABNDFILE) ... RECOVERY(NONE) -- the abend log a backout must not undo

scenarios.name: create-customer
scenarios.why: the credit check: PUT CONTAINERs CIPA-CIPE on CIPCREDCHANN, RUN TRANSID OCR1-OCR5 CHANNEL (each child a copy of the channel as it is at its RUN), DELAY FOR SECONDS(3) -- the wait at which the five children run, in RUN order, each DELAYing 1 or 2 seconds (FUNCTION RANDOM seeded by its EIBTASKN, 4243-4247) and scoring its own container -- then FETCH ANY NOSUSPEND five times (each child completed before the parent's 3 seconds: first to complete first, RUN order on a tie, X18) and GET CONTAINER of each reply channel, NOTFND RESP2 1 on the sixth, the average score and a review date; then the date of birth passes, ENQ, READ UPDATE / REWRITE of the CUSTOMER control record (customer 42 -> 43), WRITE CUSTOMER 9876540000000043, INSERT PROCTRAN 'OCC', DEQ; 'Y' with the new key

scenarios.name: born-before-1601
scenarios.why: the same credit check (five children, FETCH ANY x6), then DATE-OF-BIRTH-CHECK refuses a year before 1601 ('O') BEFORE its CEEDAYS call (the path that ends before the date service); no customer written

scenarios.name: born-in-the-future
scenarios.why: the same credit check (another five children), then DATE-OF-BIRTH-CHECK refuses a date of birth after today: 'N' / 'Y', no customer written, no PROCTRAN row

notes: CBSA's create-customer service (CRECUST, LINKed by BNK1CCS -- transaction OCCS -- with its SUBPGM-PARMS, the CRECUST copybook's layout). #4950: its credit check is the async API. It PUTs its COMMAREA into containers CIPA-CIPE of channel CIPCREDCHANN, RUNs transactions OCR1-OCR5 ("child_programs": CRDTAGY1-5, as the CSD's TRANSACTION definitions name them) with that channel, DELAYs 3 seconds, then FETCH ANY NOSUSPENDs the replies, GETs each child's container back from its reply channel, and averages the scores. The schedule is the harness's (oracle_assumptions.md X18, ASSUMED: a child runs at its parent's wait, in RUN order, and completes at its dispatch plus its own DELAYs; a task takes no processor time, X4); each child's events and the containers it leaves are compared (the CHILD event). FUNCTION RANDOM is the oracle's generator (C12) seeded by EIBTASKN: the parent's stated 4242 (X21), a child's 4242 plus its RUN number. Then the date-of-birth check, ENQ of the customer counter, the CUSTOMER control record READ UPDATE / REWRITE, the new CUSTOMER record, a PROCTRAN 'OCC' row (Db2), DEQ. CUSTOMER, ABNDFILE and PROCTRAN are compared after every scenario. Not reached: a child that does not complete within the 3 seconds (every CRDTAGY delays 1 or 2), a credit agency's failure paths, and the SYSIDERR retries (no fault can be injected on them). Data: seed.sql is cbsa-creacc's, customer.txt cbsa-custctrl's (the control record says 42 customers), both SYNTHETIC. Derived from the CICS Bank Sample Application (CBSA, github.com/cicsdev/cics-banking-sample-application-cbsa; Copyright IBM Corp. 2023), licensed under the Eclipse Public License 2.0: LICENSE here is the corpus's own; NOTICE says what is derived. #4952: CEEDAYS reads its length-10 picture and date over 8 'YYYYMMDD' bytes as their 8-byte span (oracle_assumptions.md L1: the picture characters past the last token are ASSUMED ignored, never read), and FC is the 12-byte token LE writes (L4: its 8-byte CONDITION-TOKEN-VALUE is the group inside it, not the whole). What stays named: X18, the child schedule is ASSUMED (the proof rests on it), and L1's assumption. All four scenarios run equal on the COBOL and det-port sides and every live paragraph (37 of 37) is reached. Not recorded as evidence while X18 stands; BNK1CCS, which LINKs CRECUST, is not proven by this.
